title: In Psalms 55 What Does This Psalm Teach Us About The Nature Of Prayer In Times Of Distress
paragraphs: Understanding Psalm 55: The Nature of Prayer in Times of Distress

Psalm 55 stands as a powerful expression of honest prayer in the midst of overwhelming distress. Penned by David, this psalm reveals the raw emotions of betrayal and the reality of human suffering, while simultaneously pointing us toward God as our ultimate refuge. Let us explore what this psalm teaches about the nature of prayer when we face trouble, pain, and heartache.
The Reality of Distress
David begins his prayer by urgently calling upon God:
Give ear to my prayer, O God; And hide not thyself from my supplication. Attend unto me, and answer me: I am restless in my complaint, and moan. - Psalm 55:1-2 ASV

Here, we see that prayer in distress is not sanitized or reserved. David presents his restlessness and anguish openly before God. The psalm teaches that we can—and should—bring our real emotions, fears, and anxieties to the Lord without pretense.
Honesty Before God
David does not hold back his feelings:
My heart is sore pained within me: And the terrors of death are fallen upon me. Fearfulness and trembling are come upon me, And horror hath overwhelmed me. - Psalm 55:4-5 ASV
He even expresses the desire to flee from his problems:
And I said, Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then would I fly away, and be at rest. - Psalm 55:6 ASV
The psalm validates the believer's struggle in distress and shows that expressing fear, longing, and even wishing for escape is not a lack of faith, but a part of honest prayer.
Betrayal and Personal Hurt
A unique aspect of Psalm 55 is the pain of betrayal by a close friend:

For it was not an enemy that reproached me, Then I could have borne it... But it was thou, a man mine equal, My companion, and my familiar friend. We took sweet counsel together; We walked in the house of God with the throng. - Psalm 55:12-14 ASV

This shows that prayer is not only for generic distress, but also for the deeply personal wounds of life. We are invited to bring even our most intimate pains to God, who understands betrayal and loss.
The Turning Point: Casting Our Burdens
As the psalm progresses, David moves from complaint to confidence in God's care:
As for me, I will call upon God; And Jehovah will save me. Evening, and morning, and at noonday, will I complain, and moan; And he will hear my voice. - Psalm 55:16-17 ASV
He concludes with this assurance:
Cast thy burden upon Jehovah, and he will sustain thee: He will never suffer the righteous to be moved. - Psalm 55:22 ASV

This verse is a cornerstone for understanding the nature of prayer in distress: God invites us to lay our burdens on Him, promising His sustaining strength. This aligns with New Testament teaching as well:
Casting all your anxiety upon him, because he careth for you. - 1 Peter 5:7 ASV
Christ-Centered Perspective
Ultimately, the psalm points us to Christ, who Himself experienced betrayal, sorrow, and distress in the Garden of Gethsemane:
And being in an agony he prayed more earnestly; and his sweat became as it were great drops of blood falling down upon the ground. - Luke 22:44 ASV
Jesus embodies the perfect example of taking our deepest hurts to God in prayer and trusting Him with the outcome.
Key Takeaways
Honest prayer is welcomed by God. We are encouraged to pour out our true thoughts and feelings before Him.
God is our refuge in distress. He invites us to cast our burdens upon Him, promising His sustaining power.
Betrayal and personal pain are not too small or too great for God. We can bring every wound to Him.
Persistent prayer is modeled. David prays “evening, and morning, and at noonday.”
Our hope is ultimately in God’s faithfulness. He will not let the righteous be shaken.
Conclusion

Psalm 55 teaches that prayer in times of distress is not about having the right words, but about trusting the right Person. God desires our honesty, hears our pain, and promises to sustain us. Through Christ, we are assured of His unfailing care, no matter how deep our distress.
